_note: JSON sidecar for migration-manifest.yaml. The wizard runtime CLI consumes JSON; YAML is the human-facing companion. Both files MUST stay in sync.

artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/_ext_write_sta: Now sorts flagged files by what can actually be done about them: rebuildable, not part of your live setup, already acknowledged by you, or genuinely needing a person. Only the first and last hold the project back; everything else is still listed for you.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/capability_hea: Separates two different questions: whether anything is holding the project back, and whether everything is truly normal. A file that no longer blocks is still named, and the all-clear is still withheld -- so nothing becomes invisible just because it stopped blocking.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/capability_run: New: the safe, built-in way to run a capability. The system itself opens a read-only view of your outside system and hands it to the capability, so the capability never handles a connection or a password of its own. This is what lets a capability that must look before it proposes work at all.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/lifecycle_stat: The done/completion check blocks on the same narrowed set, so it can never disagree with what turning a capability on will do.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/operator_accep: Turning a capability on now blocks only on files that really need attention, and when a file cannot be rebuilt automatically it says so plainly and offers to record your decision instead of telling you to rebuild something that cannot be rebuilt.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/read_facade.py: Refuses up front if no read-only connection was supplied, instead of failing partway through a run with a confusing technical error.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/writer_acknowl: New: where your decision is recorded when a flagged file genuinely cannot be rebuilt automatically. It keeps your own words, stays visible in the health check, and is asked again the moment that file changes -- so accepting a risk once never quietly covers a later change.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/zones.py: Marks the two new internal modules as sealed internal parts so a capability cannot import them directly.
Corrects three things on the rebuild path: the tool it told you to run was named at a location that never exists in your project; it described the order of rebuilding and turning back on backwards; and its own health checks looked at too narrow a view. It also now covers the case where a file cannot be rebuilt automatically.

migrations.migration_steps: 1. Run the update check (it reports what's new + the recommendation). 2. On the operator's yes, the assistant applies it ("${{WIZARD_HOME:-$HOME/agent-wizard}}/scripts/wizard" self-upgrade --to v0.20.0 --apply). 3. A backup is taken first; the operator's own data, rules, credentials, and logs are never touched.
migrations.notes: Minor-additive release to v0.20.0 (Cut 1.6). Fixes the one thing that could leave a project stuck with no way forward: (1) a capability that has to LOOK at your outside system before proposing changes can now do so through the safe, read-only path -- previously there was no legitimate way to do that, so such a capability could neither be rebuilt nor turned on, and the whole project stayed blocked; (2) files that are not part of your live setup (for example the tests that come with a capability) no longer hold the whole project back, though they are still listed for you; (3) if a flagged file genuinely cannot be rebuilt automatically -- because it also does something else you rely on, like sending your daily email -- the system now says so plainly and lets you record that you accept the risk of leaving it as it is, instead of telling you to rebuild something that cannot be rebuilt. That decision is kept on file, stays visible, and is asked again the moment the file changes. Anything that genuinely still needs fixing continues to block, exactly as before. No breaking changes; all existing capabilities and files are unaffected.
migrations.preflight: Verify the operator project carries a .wizard/manifest.json whose foundation_bundle_version is v0.19.0 (or any version in the supported range). A backup is taken automatically.
migrations.rollback: Restore from .wizard/backups/pre-v0.20.0/ and set foundation_bundle_version back to v0.19.0.

That decision is kept on file, stays visible, and is asked again the moment the file changes. Anything that genuinely still needs fixing continues to block, exactly as before. No breaking changes; all existing capabilities and files are unaffected.
migrations.preflight: Verify the operator project carries a .wizard/manifest.json whose foundation_bundle_version is v0.6.9 (or any version in the supported range). A backup is taken automatically.
migrations.rollback: Restore from .wizard/backups/pre-v0.20.0/ and set foundation_bundle_version back to v0.6.9.
